content: Penicillin G procaine, marketed as Bicillin C-R, should be used judiciously to prevent the emergence of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of this and other antibacterial agents. It is intended for the treatment or prevention of infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or adjustment of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform the empirical choice of treatment. This medication is specifically indicated for the treatment of moderately severe infections caused by microorganisms that are susceptible to penicillin G at serum levels achievable with this formulation. The choice of therapy should be based on bacteriological studies, including susceptibility testing, as well as the patient’s clinical response. Bicillin C-R is approved for use in both adults and pediatric patients for the following conditions: 1. Moderately severe to severe infections of the upper respiratory tract, scarlet fever, erysipelas, and skin and soft tissue infections caused by penicillin-susceptible streptococci. Streptococci belonging to Groups A, C, G, H, L, and M are highly sensitive to penicillin G. However, Group D streptococci (enterococci) are resistant to penicillin G. For streptococcal infections associated with bacteremia, penicillin G sodium or potassium is the preferred treatment. 2. Moderately severe pneumonia and otitis media caused by penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae. For severe pneumococcal infections, such as pneumonia, empyema, bacteremia, pericarditis, meningitis, peritonitis, or arthritis, penicillin G sodium or potassium is recommended during the acute phase. When high and sustained serum levels of penicillin are required, penicillin G sodium or potassium should be administered either intramuscularly (IM) or intravenously (IV). It is important to note that Bicillin C-R is not suitable for the treatment of venereal diseases, including syphilis, gonorrhea, yaws, bejel, and pinta.
